title: When the Summit Falls
premise: Salvage diver Rafael Sterling pulls a sealed chest from a river wreck the navy has quietly erased from its records, and inside finds documents proving a wartime atrocity that powerful men still alive would kill to bury. Hunted by both the navy's fixers and the descendants of the perpetrators, Rafael assembles an unlikely crew of outcasts—a disgraced archivist, a smuggler pilot, and the daughter of one of the victims—and races across the Cordillera del Viento to reach a glacier cave where the chest's twin, hidden decades ago by a dying witness, holds the proof that could finally convict them. The pass opens for only days during calving season; they must cross before the snows seal it. In the end, Rafael survives the crossing but loses his found-family patriarch to the ice, and the evidence reaches an international tribunal—justice delivered not by courts or nations, but by ordinary people who refused to forget.
about_author: Rosalind Joubert is a former maritime archaeologist who spent a decade cataloguing wrecks along contested coastlines before turning to fiction full-time. She writes adventure novels about people whom history tried to erase, drawing on fieldwork in three continents and a lifelong obsession with mountains she is legally advised not to discuss.

chapters.title: Miles, Not Years
chapters.summary: Rafael's POV. A routine dive on the sunken river freighter establishes his solitary life measured in dive-hours and river miles. He finds an anomaly on the sonar—an unlogged compartment. Emotional beat: quiet contentment shadowed by loneliness he refuses to name.

chapters.title: The Navy's Silence
chapters.summary: Rafael POV. He asks a harbor official about the wreck's registry and receives evasions, then a warning visit from a man with a naval bearing. Emotional beat: first unease—the world he trusted to ignore him is watching.

chapters.title: What the River Keeps
chapters.summary: Rafael POV. Night dive: he breaches the hidden compartment and raises a corroded chest stamped with the seal of Veloria, a nation dissolved thirty years ago. Emotional beat: awe curdling into dread as he realizes what he's holding.

chapters.title: Ash and Ledger
chapters.summary: Rafael POV. Inside: a ledger of names, dates, and cargo manifests documenting the transport of prisoners who never arrived anywhere. Emotional beat: grief for strangers, and the dawning weight of knowledge.

chapters.title: The Man Who Counts Things
chapters.summary: New POV: Elias Brandt, disgraced archivist living in exile above a bookshop. He recognizes the ledger's notation system when Rafael seeks him out through old salvage contacts. Emotional beat: two invisible men recognizing each other.

chapters.title: Veloria Was Never Real
chapters.summary: Elias POV. Elias explains Veloria: a puppet state whose archives were burned, whose crimes were absorbed into three successor governments' official silence. The men named in the ledger are now ministers and admirals. Emotional beat: fury at how cleanly history was laundered.

chapters.title: Visitors at Low Tide
chapters.summary: Rafael POV. His boat is searched while he sleeps; his dive logs are photographed. A fixer named Corven offers him money for 'the fishing equipment' he recovered. Emotional beat: fear sharpening into defiance—he lies for the first time in years.

chapters.title: The Daughter of Number Forty-One
chapters.summary: New POV: Mirena Kovač, a tribunal translator in the capital, who has spent her life chasing records of her father, listed only as Prisoner 41. She intercepts a leaked navy memo about the wreck. Emotional beat: hope arriving like a wound.

chapters.title: Three Strangers, One Chest
chapters.summary: Alternating POVs. Rafael, Elias, and Mirena meet in a border town safehouse arranged by an old smuggling contact. They pool what they know. Emotional beat: cautious trust forming—the first shape of a family none of them planned.

chapters.title: The Witness Who Walked Into Ice
chapters.summary: Elias POV. Among the ledger pages is a letter fragment referencing a 'second chest' carried over the Cordillera del Viento by a Velorian officer who vanished into the high country in the war's last winter. Emotional beat: revelation—the real proof exists, if it survived.

chapters.title: Corven's Second Offer
chapters.summary: Rafael POV. Corven escalates: threats against Elias's shop, Mirena's visa status. Rafael pretends to negotiate while buying time. Emotional beat: the cost of caring about people again.

chapters.title: The Smuggler's Map
chapters.summary: New POV briefly: Tomás Iriarte, aging pilot-smuggler, agrees to fly them to the range's southern approach—if they accept that he decides when weather grounds them. Emotional beat: gruff humor masking a man who owes a debt to the dead of Veloria.

chapters.title: Leaving the Water
chapters.summary: Rafael POV. He scuttles his own boat to fake his death and abandons the only home he's had in three years. Emotional beat: mourning a self he built to stay invisible.

chapters.title: Flight Over the Foothills
chapters.summary: Tomás POV. The flight south, pursued once by a navy aircraft that turns back at the range's edge. Banter, maps, and the first sight of the Cordillera. Emotional beat: exhilaration—the crew becoming a crew.

chapters.title: The Town That Forgot Its Name
chapters.summary: Mirena POV. Last settlement before the pass; an old woman recognizes the Velorian seal and tells of soldiers who came through in winter 'carrying a box heavier than a coffin.' Emotional beat: memory persisting where archives failed.

chapters.title: Calving Season
chapters.summary: Elias POV. Local guides explain the glacier route: the calving season destabilizes the icefall, opening a brief corridor through the seracs—days, not weeks. After the snows, nothing passes until spring. Emotional beat: the clock starts.

chapters.title: The Guide Who Says No
chapters.summary: Rafael POV. Every guide refuses the route; one, Sefa Anand, finally agrees—not for money, but because her grandfather guided the Velorian officer and never spoke of what happened after. Emotional beat: inherited guilt finding purpose.

chapters.title: First Ascent, First Loss
chapters.summary: Sefa POV. The climb begins; a storm forces them into a bivouac and Tomás's heart gives him trouble. They leave caches and mark the route. Emotional beat: fragility of bodies against the mountain's indifference.

chapters.title: Corven Follows
chapters.summary: Rafael POV. Radio intercept: Corven has hired ex-military trackers and entered the foothills. The hunters are days behind and better equipped. Emotional beat: paranoia on the ice—every sound is footsteps.

chapters.title: The Icefall Corridor
chapters.summary: Sefa POV. Calving season opens the route: a cathedral of leaning seracs that groan and shift hourly. They move at dawn in silence. Emotional beat: terror transfigured into something like reverence.

chapters.title: Prisoner 41's Name
chapters.summary: Mirena POV. At a high camp, cross-referencing the ledger with the old woman's account, Elias reconstructs the officer's identity—and Mirena learns her father's true name and that he helped carry the second chest. Emotional beat: a father restored to her, thirty years late.

chapters.title: Whiteout
chapters.summary: Rafael POV. A two-day whiteout pins them in a snow cave; rations run short; Tomás worsens. Confessions surface around the stove—why each of them stayed invisible. Emotional beat: the found family becomes real in the dark.

chapters.title: The Officer's Camp
chapters.summary: Sefa POV. They find the 1940s campsite preserved in ice: a skeleton, a rusted rifle, and a carved marker in Velorian. The officer made it this far. Emotional beat: communion with the dead who led them here.

chapters.title: Contact
chapters.summary: Rafael POV. First exchange of fire with Corven's trackers on a moraine; they escape by traversing an unstable slope, losing most of their supplies. Emotional beat: survival bought with everything comfortable.

chapters.title: The Cave Beneath the Glacier
chapters.summary: Elias POV. Following the officer's carved bearings, they find a melt-cave behind the icefall—and inside, a bronze-bound chest, frozen in place for thirty years. Emotional beat: disbelief, then tears; the dead kept their promise.

chapters.title: What Cannot Be Burned
chapters.summary: Mirena POV. The chest holds film, photographs, and the officer's testimony naming every perpetrator—including Corven's patron, Admiral Vess. Enough for a tribunal. Not enough copies to survive a single fire. Emotional beat: triumph shadowed by responsibility.

chapters.title: Vess Moves
chapters.summary: New POV: Admiral Vess in the capital, ordering Corven to ensure no one crosses back—'the mountain can be blamed.' Emotional beat: cold institutional evil, banal and certain.

chapters.title: The Corridor Closes
chapters.summary: Sefa POV. Early storm signals the calving window shutting early. They have hours, not days, and Corven's team between them and the descent. Emotional beat: dread compressing into resolve.

chapters.title: Running the Seracs
chapters.summary: Rafael POV. Descent through the collapsing icefall as calving begins—seracs toppling, the route erasing itself behind them. A near-death traverse Rafael barely leads them through. Emotional beat: adrenaline, prayer, and leadership he never asked for.

chapters.title: Ambush at the Moraine
chapters.summary: Multiple POVs. Corven's trackers catch them in the open. Standoff; Tomás creates a diversion using their flare cache and is fatally shot covering the others' escape. Emotional beat: grief and rage—the first member of the family lost.

chapters.title: What Tomás Owed
chapters.summary: Elias POV. In Tomás's jacket they find a letter: he was the soldier ordered to burn the Velorian archive and refused, fleeing instead. He'd been running toward this redemption for thirty years. Emotional beat: mourning transformed into inheritance.

chapters.title: The Long Way Down
chapters.summary: Sefa POV. Wounded, short on food, they take Sefa's secret emergency route—a vertical gully only she knows. Three days of climbing. Emotional beat: endurance as love; each carrying another's weight literally.

chapters.title: Corven's End
chapters.summary: Rafael POV. Corven corners them at the gully mouth—but the mountain settles, taking his team in an avalanche he triggered carelessly. Rafael saves Corven from the ice, then lets justice, not vengeance, decide: they bind him and bring him down as witness. Emotional beat: mercy as the harder choice.

chapters.title: Snowbound Village
chapters.summary: Mirena POV. They reach the far-side village as snows close the pass entirely—trapped together for weeks, but safe, with the evidence copied four ways. Emotional beat: exhausted peace; laughter returning.

chapters.title: Testimony
chapters.summary: Elias POV. From the village radio office, Mirena transmits authenticated copies to the tribunal, three newspapers, and the victims' descendants' association. There is no way now to burn it all. Emotional beat: the moment invisibility ends on purpose.

chapters.title: The Tribunal Summons
chapters.summary: Rafael POV. Spring comes; the pass reopens; they descend to summonses waiting—Vess arrested, Corven testifying, Rafael called as finder of fact. Emotional beat: anxiety giving way to steadiness; he chooses to be seen.

chapters.title: Names Read Aloud
chapters.summary: Mirena POV. At the hearing, the ledger's names are read into the record, including Prisoner 41's restored name. Survivors' families fill the gallery. Emotional beat: catharsis—memory winning over erasure.

chapters.title: Sentences and Silences
chapters.summary: Elias POV. Verdicts land: convictions for some, outraging acquittals for others—but the archive is public forever, and Elias is offered his chair back and declines it. Emotional beat: justice outside the law proving more durable than justice within it.

chapters.title: The River Again
chapters.summary: Rafael POV. Rafael returns to the river and dives the wreck one last time, leaving a memorial plaque with the prisoners' names bolted to the hull. Emotional beat: closure without forgetting; grief integrated.

chapters.title: A Crew Worth Keeping
chapters.summary: Ensemble POV. One year later: Rafael, Mirena, Elias, and Sefa launch a small foundation documenting erased histories from a converted salvage boat—Tomás's name painted on the wheelhouse. Emotional beat: warmth; the found family sails on, visible at last.
